name: PING: Physicists Inspiring the Next Generation (FRIB, Michigan State University)
org: Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), Michigan State University
what_you_do: Spend two weeks learning nuclear physics at the FRIB lab with college student mentors. It can turn into a year-long research project, and students present their work at science conferences.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 at a U.S. high school, or a high school in the U.S. territories or Freely Associated States. Middle school students can ask through the contact form. You need a reference from a teacher or coach.
pay_detail: Free. PING covers housing, meals and a flight for students from out of state. Bring a little spending money for outings. It does not pay a wage.
duration: 2 weeks in the summer (2026: July 12 to 25, run online that year)
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was March 15, 2026, and the program ran July 12 to 25, 2026. The 2027 deadline is not posted yet. Decisions for 2027 will be sent by May 1, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply on the PING website (nsbping.org) when the 2027 application is posted. Name a teacher or coach as your reference, and they get an email asking for it. About 20 to 24 students are picked. Questions: ping@frib.msu.edu.
notes: Read on the PING site (linked from the FRIB high school page) in a browser on 2026-10-16. PING 2027 takes grades 9 to 11, not 12. The FAQ calls it a free residential program, but PING 2026 was run online, so check how 2027 will run. The 2026 deadline and dates come from the MSU Spartan Youth listing. Not a paid job.
